nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $\mathrm{indep}$ be an independence system on the finite subsets of $\alpha$ for which the greedy algorithm is optimal. If $I$ and $J$ are independent sets with $|I| < |J|$, then some element $e \in J$ with $e \notin I$ makes $I \cup \{e\}$ independent.
nodes.title: Greedy optimality gives the augmentation axiom

Let $L$ be a list of elements of $\alpha$ in nonincreasing order of weight (whenever $a$ occurs before $b$ in $L$, $w(b) \le w(a)$), and let $G$ be the set returned by the greedy algorithm with oracle $O$ on…
nodes.title: Threshold counts of the matroid greedy result

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $\mathrm{indep}$ be an independence system on the finite subsets of $\alpha$ for which the greedy algorithm is optimal. Then there is a matroid $M$ on $\alpha$ whose ground set is all of $\alpha$ such that a finite set $S \subseteq \alpha$ is independent in $M$ exactly when $S$ is independent under $\mathrm{indep}$.
nodes.title: Greedy-optimal independence systems are matroids

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $\mathrm{indep}$ be an independence system on the finite subsets of $\alpha$. The greedy algorithm is optimal for $\mathrm{indep}$ if and only if there is a matroid $M$ on $\alpha$ whose ground set is all of $\alpha$ such that a finite set $S \subseteq \alpha$ is independent in $M$ exactly when $S$ is independent under $\mathrm{indep}$.
nodes.title: Rado–Edmonds theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $\mathrm{indep}$ be an independence oracle on the finite subsets of $\alpha$. The greedy algorithm is optimal for $\mathrm{indep}$ when, for every weight function $w : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ and every list $L$ that contains every element of $\alpha$ exactly once, in nonincreasing order of $w$, the set $T$ returned by the matroid greedy algorithm on $L$ with oracle…
nodes.title: Greedy optimality

nodes.summary: A predicate $\mathrm{indep}$ on the finite subsets of a type $\alpha$ is an independence system when the empty set is independent and every subset of an independent set is independent.
nodes.title: Independence system

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid on a type $\alpha$ and let $O$ be an oracle that accepts a finite set $A \subseteq \alpha$ exactly when $A$ is independent in $M$. For every list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$, the set returned by the greedy algorithm with oracle $O$ on $L$ is independent in $M$, and each of its elements occurs in $L$.
nodes.title: The matroid greedy result is independent

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid on a type $\alpha$ with ground set $E$, and let $O$ be an oracle that accepts a finite set $A \subseteq \alpha$ exactly when $A$ is independent in $M$. For every list $L$ in which an element of $\alpha$ occurs if and only if it lies in $E$, the set returned by the greedy algorithm with oracle $O$ on $L$ is a base of $M$.
nodes.title: The matroid greedy result is a base

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid on a type $\alpha$, let $O$ be an oracle that accepts a finite set $A \subseteq \alpha$ exactly when $A$ is independent in $M$, and let $w : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ be a weight function. Let $L$ be a list of elements of $\alpha$ in nonincreasing order of weight (whenever $a$ occurs before $b$ in $L$, $w(b) \le w(a)$), and let $G$ be the set returned by the greedy algorithm with oracle $O$ on…
nodes.title: Optimality of the matroid greedy algorithm

nodes.summary: For every oracle $O$ on finite subsets of a type $\alpha$, every finite set $S \subseteq \alpha$ and all lists $P$ and $Q$ of elements of $\alpha$, the set returned by the greedy scan with oracle $O$ from $S$ over $P$ followed by $Q$ equals the set returned by the greedy scan with oracle $O$ over $Q$ starting from the set that the scan with oracle $O$ from $S$ over $P$ returns.
nodes.title: The greedy scan over a concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $\mathrm{indep}$ be an independence oracle on the finite subsets of $\alpha$, let $S$ be a finite subset of $\alpha$ and let $L$ be a list of elements of $\alpha$ such that $\mathrm{indep}$ rejects $S \cup \{e\}$ for every $e$ in $L$. Then the greedy scan of $L$ starting from $S$ returns $S$.
nodes.title: A scan that accepts nothing

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $\mathrm{indep}$ be an independence system on the finite subsets of $\alpha$ and let $I$ be an independent set. For every list $L$ of elements of $I$ and every finite set $S \subseteq I$, the greedy scan of $L$ starting from $S$ returns $S$ together with all elements of $L$.
nodes.title: A scan inside an independent set keeps everything

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid on a type $\alpha$, let $O$ be an oracle that accepts a finite set $A \subseteq \alpha$ exactly when $A$ is independent in $M$, let $S$ be a finite independent set of $M$ and $L$ a list of elements of $\alpha$, and let $T$ be the set returned by the greedy scan with oracle $O$ from $S$ over $L$. Then $T$ is independent in $M$, and for every element $e$ of $L$ with $e \notin T$, the set…
nodes.title: Invariant of the greedy scan

nodes.summary: For every oracle $O$ on finite subsets of a type $\alpha$, every finite set $S \subseteq \alpha$ and every list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$, the greedy scan with oracle $O$ from $S$ over $L$ takes time exactly the length of $L$.
nodes.title: Running time of the greedy scan

nodes.summary: Given an oracle $O$ that accepts or rejects each finite subset of a type $\alpha$, a finite set $S \subseteq \alpha$ and a list $e_1, \dots, e_n$ of elements of $\alpha$, the greedy scan processes $e_1, \dots, e_n$ in order, starting with $S$ as the current set: it replaces the current set $T$ by $T \cup \{e_i\}$ if $O$ accepts $T \cup \{e_i\}$, and leaves it unchanged otherwise. It returns the final current set…
nodes.title: Greedy scan with an independence oracle

nodes.summary: For every oracle $O$ on finite subsets of a type $\alpha$ and every list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$, the greedy algorithm with oracle $O$ on $L$ takes time exactly the length of $L$, one oracle query per element.
nodes.title: Running time of the matroid greedy algorithm

nodes.summary: Given an oracle $O$ that accepts or rejects each finite subset of a type $\alpha$ and a list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$, the greedy algorithm starts from the empty set, processes the elements of $L$ in order, adds an element $e$ to the current set $T$ when $O$ accepts $T \cup \{e\}$ and leaves $T$ unchanged otherwise, and returns the final set. It charges one unit of time per element processed.
nodes.title: Greedy algorithm on a matroid

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
